notes: Downloaded 2026-08-25 to ignored data_lock/raw directory; gzip/zip N/A (plain TSV), integrity confirmed by successful full parse. PRIDE API (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/ws/archive/v2/projects/PXD055821/files, 174 total files) confirmed this is one of two small DIA-NN output matrices for a sub-cohort of the full project (the other, 220920_PN_CRC_LM_all_63_LM_DIANN.pg_matrix.tsv, a protein-group-level file, is available from PRIDE but was not downloaded/not used -- this gene-group-level file is the one actually used). The remaining ~150 raw .raw files (~1GB each) and two Proteome Discoverer .pdResult/.msf files (44-54GB) are not usable in this environment (no MaxQuant/Proteome Discoverer/search-engine software available) and were not downloaded -- confirmed via HEAD/API metadata only, not full listing verified file-by-file. The 60 columns correspond to the publication's own "Sydney cohort" -- independently confirmed 2026-08-25 (PR #82 round 1 review) by fetching the publication's own full text (PMC12335997, DOI 10.1016/J.MCPRO.2025.101026): "the third cohort was from the tumor bank of the Kolling Institute, Royal North Shore Hospital in Sydney, Australia and comprised 60 specimens collected from 51 patients... samples of the third cohort were processed and measured [by DIA-NN] at the Kolling Institute." Full project total is 152 specimens from 111 patients across three centers (UKSH 42/42, UKE 50/18, Sydney 60/51); only the Sydney sub-cohort's small DIA-NN matrix is used here. Filename says "all_63_LM" but the matrix has exactly 60 columns -- consistent with the publication's own stated Sydney-cohort size of 60 specimens, so the "63" is very likely stale/mismatched naming from an earlier draft of the run rather than an unexplained data-content gap; the reason for the stale filename itself remains unresolved. Columns are specimens, not independent patients (60 specimens from 51 patients -- some patients contributed more than one specimen, exact per-patient breakdown not stated in the fetched text and not resolved further); column-to-patient mapping has not been reconstructed here -- header carries only the original DIA-NN run file paths (e.g. "H:\Paula\CRC_LM\...\220624_CRCLM_PN_S24.mzML"), not patient IDs. Every "n/60" figure this dataset's evidence rows report is therefore a specimen-level detection fraction, not a patient-level prevalence. 9,263 gene rows; all five A_CLINICAL targets (CEACAM5, ERBB2, F3, NECTIN4, TACSTD2) confirmed present by exact gene-symbol match.
